newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan military to grill UNITA prisoners in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Angolan military to grill UNITA prisoners in Zaire.

text.p: Angolan military officials have been sent to Zaire's second city Lubumbashi to interrogate soldiers from Angola's UNITA movement taken prisoner by Zaire rebels, a senior Angolan government official said on Friday.
"(Rebel leader Laurent) Kabila called us on this last week and we have dispatched a team to Lubumbashi to interview these people," Angola's deputy foreign minister George Chicoty told Reuters.

"They (prisoners) were fighting alongside Interhamwe when they were captured, but I don't know where they were captured in Zaire," Chicoty added, referring to Rwandan militia fighting Kabila's forces, who control three-quarters of the country.

Kabila, who began the armed struggle in October to topple Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, has visited neighbouring Angola at least twice since March for talks with President Jose Eduardo dos Santos on the conflict.
UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi is a close ally of Mobutu, who allowed the movement to set up food and weapons supply bases in Zaire during Angola's 20-year civil war, which ended in 1994.

Chicoty said the Angolan government had earlier estimated the number of UNITA troops involved in the Zaire conflict at around 5,000, but he said more recent estimates put the numbers closer to 15,000.
UNITA has denied involvement in Zaire.
"These reports are unfounded and senseless," UNITA's number two in parliament, Isaias Samakuva told Reuters.
"Every time Kabila finds some resistance, UNITA troops are said to be involved . Even the Zaire army, at some point, is capable of putting up a fight," he said.
Samakuva said the Angolan government was supporting the rebels in Zaire with men and logistics.

"As for the government...they are quite deeply involved. Just a few days ago some very high ranking officers of the FAA (Angolan Armed Forces) were in Zaire. We know for a fact they have been supporting the rebels with men and logistics for a long time," he said.
Chicoty, who is also head of the small opposition Angolan Democratic Forum party, said Angolan government troops were massed in two positions at the Zairean border.
"There is a crisis in Zaire and we have every right to defend our borders," Chicoty said.
He said troops were concentrated in the south of the Cabinda enclave and in the northeastern Lunda Norte province at the northern border town of Dundo.
